title: The members of Armstrong's All-Stars
summary: He lists Cozy Cole or Big Sid Catlett, Jack Teagarden, Dick Carey or Earl Hines, Arvell Shaw and Velma Middleton, and values having played with two of the greatest.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: When I met you, you were with Louie and there was a five-piece band. Who were the other people? You said a seven-piece band.
Let's see. We had a drummer -- we had Cozy Cole at one time -- No, Big Sid, Teagarden. That's two. Who was playing piano? Oh, --
Earl was when I met you.

Yeah, but he wasn't -- I'm talking about the first band. Dick Carey played the piano. That's three. I played clarinet. That's four. And Arvell Shaw played bass. That's five. And, let's see, and Velma Middleton was six. She was the vocalist. That's about it, six.
There was Earl and you and Jack Teagarden and Big Sid and Louie and Arvell and Velma.
Yeah, I didn't count Louie. Louie is seven; with the vocalist, that's six and Louie made it seven.
Louie and you and Earl, Arvell and Big Sid and Jack Teagarden.
But I enjoyed both of them. I know one thing, it's a wonderful experience. You couldn't buy it. To be known as
being one of the guys that played with two of the greatest. So what more can you ask for, huh?
